title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:

【Introduction · section-2-p3】Advancements in big data and computing have expanded the application of machine learning in medicine. Machine learning techniques can analyze complex clinical data to identify prognostic markers and create predictive models.8 Techniques such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) can explain the contributions of factors to model predictions,9 aiding clinicians in treatment optimization. This study aimed to develop an interpretable prognostic model for HBOT, by integrating predictive analytics with explainable artificial intelligence, with the goal of personalizing treatment regimens, reducing inefficiencies, and enhancing patient outcomes, ultimately providing valuable clinical insights in intracerebral hemorrhage patients.

【Introduction · section-2-p1】Intracerebral hemorrhage is a severe cerebrovascular event with high mortality rates, comprising 10–15% of all strokes.1 Current evidence suggests that the hematoma, cerebral edema, and neuroinflammatory after intracerebral hemorrhage often result in severe neurological deficits and death.23 Surgical craniotomy, catheter drainage, and conservative management have demonstrated limited efficacy in the survival and prognosis of intracerebral hemorrhage patients. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more effective treatment strategies.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Data collection · section-5-p1】We collected comprehensive patient data from the Hospital Information System, including demographic characteristics (age, gender), medical history (hypertension, diabetes, anticoagulant use), etiology of cerebral hemorrhage (spontaneous, traumatic), treatment modalities (conservative, surgical), surgical approaches (craniotomy, minimally invasive), surgical details (operation time, intraoperative blood loss), admission status (Glasgow coma scale (GCS), activities of daily living (ADL), hemiplegia, aphasia), neuroimaging findings (hemorrhage location, volume), bleeding sites (basal ganglia, thalamus, cerebral lobe, brainstem, cerebellum, subarachnoid hemorrhage, subdural space, epidural space, intravascular hemolysis (IVH)), laboratory values (white blood cell count, hemoglobin count, platelet count, prothrombin time, international normalized ratio, activated partial thromboplastin time, D-dimer, alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase, albumin, potassium concentration, sodium concentration, calcium concentration, serum creatinine, uric acid, blood glucose), HBOT (timing, frequency), reasons for treatment interruption, HBOT-related complications (oxygen toxicity, barotrauma), other clinical complications (rebleeding, infection, thrombosis, epilepsy), and long-term outcomes (ADL at discharge, intensive care unit/hospital length of stay, 3-month mRS).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Development and validation of a machine learning-based predictive model for prognosis in cerebral hemorrhage patients after hyperbaric oxygen therapy》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Construction and validation of the prediction model · section-7-p2】The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve is used to evaluate the overall performance of binary classification models.11 By varying classification thresholds, the dynamic relationship between the true positive rate (sensitivity) and the false positive rate (1 − specificity) is calculated, and the ROC curve is plotted to compute the area under the curve (AUC). By comparing the AUC values of different models, the model’s ability to distinguish between positive and negative classes is quantified, and the optimal threshold is determined based on the ROC curve to balance sensitivity and specificity.

【Establishment and validation of the prediction model · section-11-p1】Logistic regression analysis identified independent factors significantly associated with poor prognosis. The predictive ability of selected algorithms was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. The 10-fold cross-validation receiver operating characteristic curves showed the prediction results for various models: logistic regression (AUC = 0.98), support vector machines (AUC = 0.97), K-nearest neighbors (AUC = 0.96), multilayer perceptron (AUC = 0.97), naive Bayes (AUC = 0.97), decision tree (AUC = 0.96), random forest (AUC = 0.99), and gradient boosting (AUC = 0.98; Figure 2).

【Figure 2 · mgr.MEDGASRES-D-25-00168-F2】Figure 2 The comparison of ROC curves for eight different machine learning models for classification.The random forest model performed best (AUC = 0.99), followed by logistic regression and gradient boosting (AUC = 0.98). AUC: Area under the curve; k-MN: k-nearest neighbors; MLP: multi-layer perceptron; ROC: receiver operating characteristic; SVM: support vector machine.
